Best macOS Accessibility permission apps: Gojo, Rectangle, Raycast, Maccy, and more

Accessibility permission is common in serious Mac utilities because window management, keyboard automation, and other workflow tools often need deeper system access. This guide explains where Gojo fits among popular Mac apps.

Updated July 2, 20269 min readAll posts

Short answer

If you want one broad MacBook notch surface, start with Gojo. If you only need one specialist job, pick the specialist: Rectangle for window snapping, Maccy for clipboard history, AltTab for window switching, f.lux for display warmth, Raycast for keyboard commands, BetterTouchTool for automation, or Karabiner-Elements for keyboard remapping.

  • Best broad workflow: Gojo for media, windows, clipboard, files, calendar, battery, webcam, and display controls in the notch.
  • Best specialist tools: Rectangle, Maccy, AltTab, f.lux, Raycast, BetterTouchTool, and Karabiner-Elements for focused jobs.
  • Permission rule: grant Accessibility only when the feature actually needs window, keyboard, or UI control.
On this pageQuick picksComparison tableMethodologyFAQ

Quick picks

  1. RectangleGojo vs Rectangle: which Mac window tool fits your workflow?Choose Rectangle if fast, dedicated keyboard shortcuts and snap areas are the main thing you want from window management.
  2. f.luxGojo vs f.lux: MacBook notch controls or adaptive display lighting?Choose f.lux if your main need is a dedicated, location- and wake-time-aware display-lighting schedule.
  3. Boring NotchGojo vs Boring Notch: which MacBook notch utility fits your workflow?Choose Boring Notch if you want an expanded notch centered on music playback controls and a visualizer.
  4. AltTabGojo vs AltTab: Mac window switching or a notch workspace?Choose AltTab if your main friction is switching among individual windows and you value dedicated switcher controls, previews, filters, and shortcuts.
  5. MaccyGojo vs Maccy: clipboard history or a broader Mac utility?Choose Maccy if you want a focused clipboard-history app with search, keyboard-first use, pinned items, and local storage.
  6. RaycastGojo vs Raycast: MacBook notch controls or a keyboard-first launcher?Choose Raycast if your workflow begins with a keyboard shortcut, search, commands, extensions, snippets, and automation across apps and services.
  7. BetterTouchToolGojo vs BetterTouchTool: notch utility or deep Mac automation?Choose BetterTouchTool when your priority is designing custom gestures, shortcuts, triggers, and multi-step automations across your Mac.
  8. Karabiner-ElementsGojo vs Karabiner-Elements: MacBook notch utility or keyboard remapper?Choose Karabiner-Elements when the problem is your keyboard: remapping a key, adapting an external keyboard, or applying detailed conditional rules.

Comparison table

RaycastKeyboard-first launcher and command interfacePeople who want to search, launch, automate, and use extensions without leaving the keyboardGojo favors hoverable, glanceable access in the MacBook notch.
BetterTouchToolConfigurable input customization and automationPeople who want to assign actions to gestures, keys, mice, Touch Bar, or other triggersGojo is more focused on immediate notch-based utility access.
Karabiner-ElementsKeyboard customization and key remappingUsers who need keys to send different keys or mouse-button eventsGojo does not compete on low-level keyboard remapping.

How Gojo fits the Accessibility permission space

Many serious Mac utilities touch the Accessibility permission ecosystem because they need to observe windows, move windows, remap inputs, or automate parts of the interface. Gojo should be evaluated the same way: ask which features need deeper access, whether the request matches the job, and whether the app is transparent about what it changes.

Gojo is strongest when you want a MacBook notch surface for several daily workflows at once. It is not the best answer when you only need one specialist utility with deep configuration.

Methodology and source notes

This roundup is organized by workflow fit, permission scope, and how directly each app solves a Mac utility problem. It favors official product pages and documentation over broad claims, then links each comparison page for deeper context.

  • Official sources checked on July 2, 2026: Rectangle, f.lux, Boring Notch, AltTab, Maccy, Raycast, BetterTouchTool, Karabiner-Elements, and Gojo project pages.
  • The recommendations are fit-based, not absolute rankings; several tools can run together when their shortcuts and permissions do not conflict.

FAQ

Are macOS Accessibility permission apps safe?

They can be, but the permission is powerful. Grant it only to apps you trust, and prefer tools with clear documentation, active maintenance, and a reason that matches their feature set.

Why do Mac utilities ask for Accessibility permission?

Window managers, keyboard tools, launchers, and automation utilities may need Accessibility access to observe or control windows, keyboard events, or system UI behavior.

Is Gojo an Accessibility app?

Gojo is a Mac utility that may participate in the Accessibility permission ecosystem for specific workflow features. It is not a replacement for Apple’s built-in assistive technologies.

Which Mac utility should I install first?

Install the tool that matches the recurring friction. Use Gojo for a notch workspace, Rectangle for snapping, Maccy for clipboard history, AltTab for switching, and Raycast for command-palette workflows.
